root_idea.summary: The root centers on fright and on the heart or mind as the place where fright settles.
root_idea.development: From fear as an inner state, the lexicon develops uses for causing fear, taking someone by surprise, inspiring awe or admiration, and describing sharp or lively responsiveness. These extensions belong to particular lexical forms and are not all meanings of the Quranic noun.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic noun is presented under the normalized classical citation form رَوْعٌ.

senses.definition: Fright or fear that has seized or affected the heart or mind.
senses.usage_conditions: A noun for fear as an experienced inner state; in 11:74, it is the fright that departed from Abraham.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To frighten, terrify, or make afraid; to cause fear to reach someone's heart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive; also said of an affair, event, or thing that frightens. Impressive beauty, abundance, or multitude may be the cause. Passive and intransitive forms mean to become frightened or afraid.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take by surprise; to come upon someone suddenly or unexpectedly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional extension of striking the heart or mind, used of an unforeseen arrival or encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To excite admiration and approval, pleasure, or joy; to possess a beauty or excellence that produces this response.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Both transitive and intransitive uses are attested. The response may arise from beauty, pleasing appearance, courage, or excellence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cool the heart or allay its thirst.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare poetic use, especially of a draught that relieves the heart's thirst.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be stirred to alacrity and cheerfulness, inclining one to do good promptly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In اِرْتَاعَ لِلْخَيْرِ, to be disposed toward and love doing good.
A tropical noun use, as in witnessing or being present at war or battle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The heart or mind; the seat of fear, and by extension the understanding or intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in constructions meaning that something entered one's mind or was inspired into one's heart; it can also occur in idioms concerning the heart's return or composure.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The quality of exciting admiration and approval through beauty, pleasing appearance, or courage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An abstract noun describing the quality associated with the impressive epithet أَرْوَعُ or رَوْعَاءُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A fit or episode of fright or fear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may denote a sudden fright, including fright caused to people by horsemen or to an animal by an alarming encounter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A trait, sign, or mark of beauty; beauty that excites admiration, pleasure, or joy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A visible quality that affects the heart of the beholder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Quick, spirited, vigorous, and sharp in spirit; of a heart, easily startled by what is heard or seen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: رُوَاعُ الفُؤَادِ and رُوَاعَةُ الفُؤَادِ are applied to a she-camel or mare in the quick-spirited sense, not to a male in that use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Frightening or making afraid, especially by impressive beauty, abundance, or multitude.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active-participle adjective; an impressive appearance may inspire fear or awe.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Beautiful, impressive, or pleasing, exciting admiration and approval.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person, horse, ornament, speech, or similar object; courage, excellence, and pleasing appearance are among the attested grounds of admiration.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person of striking beauty or impressive presence who excites admiration; in a reported usage, sharp and lively in spirit or intellect.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The epithet has the feminine رَوْعَاءُ and may describe imposing stature, presence, or lively intelligence.
A possessive or passive adjectival use, also associated with the form رَوِعٌ; the active form may be analyzed as having passive force in this use.
